content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Define the mole as a unit of amount of substance
State the value of Avogadro's constant
Understand the relationship between moles, mass, and Mr
Atoms and molecules are incredibly small, and even tiny samples contain enormous numbers of particles. The
is a counting unit that allows chemists to work with manageable numbers when dealing with atoms, molecules, and other particles.
(symbol: mol) is the SI unit for
One mole of any substance contains exactly the same number of particles (atoms, molecules, ions, etc.).
1 mole of carbon atoms = 6.02 × 10²³ carbon atoms
1 mole of water molecules = 6.02 × 10²³ water molecules
1 mole of sodium ions = 6.02 × 10²³ sodium ions
A single carbon atom has a mass of about 2 × 10⁻²³ g
This is far too small to measure practically
Relate numbers of particles to mass
The Link Between Moles, Mass, and Mr
One mole of any substance has a mass equal to its relative formula mass (Mr) in grams.
The relationship between moles, mass, and molar mass:
M = molar mass (g/mol), which equals Mr
[DIAGRAM: Triangle showing n, m, M relationship]
To find the number of particles:
Calculate the number of moles in 36 g of water (H₂O).
Calculate the mass of 0.5 mol of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃).
Calculate the number of molecules in 2 mol of carbon dioxide.
3.2 g of sulfur contains 0.1 mol. Calculate the molar mass and identify if this is S or S₈.
Since Ar of S = 32, and molar mass = 32 g/mol, this must be sulfur atoms (S), not S₈ molecules (which would have M = 256 g/mol).
How many atoms are in 6 g of carbon?
Moles of Atoms vs Moles of Molecules
Be careful about what you're counting:
1 mol of O atoms = 6.02 × 10²³ oxygen atoms (mass = 16 g)
1 mol of O₂ molecules = 6.02 × 10²³ oxygen molecules (mass = 32 g)
1 mol of O₂ molecules contains 2 mol of O atoms
Always include units in your calculations:
Mr has no units; molar mass has units of g/mol (but numerically equal)
Forgetting to calculate Mr before using the formula
Always calculate Mr from the formula first
Confusing moles of atoms with moles of molecules
Be clear about what particles you're counting

Calculate the number of molecules in 9 g of water. (3 marks)
A sample contains 3.01 × 10²³ atoms of iron. Calculate the mass of the sample. (Ar of Fe = 56) (3 marks)
The SI unit of amount of substance; contains 6.02 × 10²³ particles
The number of particles in one mole: 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹
The mass of one mole of a substance, in g/mol
is the unit for amount of substance
Mass of 1 mole = Mr in grams
Always be clear about whether you're counting atoms, molecules, or ions
